hypothesis: The compiled native Type-C adapter attaches and detaches in both cable orientations and holds VCONN off with the correct role and power delay, under single-core and SMP configurations.

conditions.toolchain: pinned local toolchain, FreeRTOS sources, Python Unicorn and pyelftools

conclusion: Passed on the host model; electrical admission and physical operation are unqualified.
narrative: checks/a733-typec-native.py (removed as a modeled native Type-C composition with saved fault checkpoints; it refused to overwrite an evidence directory and was run with --output DIR) covered the original fixed-host composition with the actual native Type-C, TWI, PMIC, pin, rail, clock, counter, translation and lock implementations. FreeRTOS task/queue behavior, MMIO responses and electrical qualification were modeled. Both cable orientations completed attachment and detach. Saved execution checkpoints also covered pre-pin authority loss, external VBUS refusal, retained I2C failure, stale observation, invalid tokens and brief registry contention; delayed STOP completion preserved the observation's request-start timestamp. The compiled native adapter passed both single-core and SMP configuration checks. The executed trace preserved S_TWI0's shared clock/reset bits, selected 100 kHz I2C, held VCONN off, selected source/data-host role, and waited more than 120 ms before enabling power. The initial execution reached its instruction cap during normal interrupt configuration; it resumed from preserved CPU, memory and modeled-hardware state on the same executable without replaying startup and successful cases. The canonical runner used the established bounded allowance; its trace assertions were checked against the preserved execution without another emulation run.
